name: position: static
desc: The default. The box stays in normal flow and every offset is ignored.

name: relative as a containing block
desc: Keeps the box in flow and makes it the containing block for absolute children. With no offsets it looks unchanged.
body: Use `relative` with no offsets when the only goal is to anchor a child. Adding `top: 2px` also shifts the painted box and can hide a border, so keep the two jobs separate.

name: absolute stretch with inset
desc: Removes the box from flow and stretches it to its containing block when width and height stay auto.

name: absolute centering
syntax: .modal { position: absolute; inset: 0; margin: auto; width: 320px; height: 200px; }
desc: Sets all four offsets plus auto margins, so the fixed size box centers on both axes.

name: fixed header
desc: Pins the header to the top of the viewport. The body must reserve the same height or the first content slides under it.
body: A `transform`, `filter`, `perspective` or `contain: paint` on an ancestor makes that ancestor the containing block, and the header scrolls with the page. Check the wrapper before adding more `z-index`.

name: sticky table header
desc: Keeps the header row visible inside a scrolling table or list without JavaScript.

name: why sticky does nothing
desc: Sticky needs a threshold, a taller parent, and no clipping ancestor between it and the scrollport.

name: inset
desc: Shorthand for the four offsets. Values follow the same order as margin.

name: finding the containing block
desc: An absolute box measures against the padding box of the nearest ancestor whose position is not static, or the initial containing block.

name: isolation: isolate
desc: Creates a stacking context with no visual side effect, so a component's internal z-index values stay inside it.

name: z-index scale with custom properties
desc: Keeps layer values in one place so a new component can be inserted between two existing ones.

name: viewport meta tag
desc: Makes the layout viewport match the device width. Without it a phone renders at about 980px and zooms out.
example:
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<!-- No maximum-scale and no user-scalable=no: both block pinch zoom. -->
body: Test the result at 375px wide. With the tag in place, `100vw` is 375px and a `min-width: 48em` query does not match, which is what the mobile layout expects.

name: mobile first layout
desc: Base styles describe the narrow screen and min-width queries add columns as space appears.

name: em breakpoints
desc: Breakpoints in em follow the user's font size and zoom. One em inside a query is the initial font size, normally 16px.

name: fluid type with clamp()
desc: Scales a heading with the viewport inside fixed limits. The preferred value mixes rem and vw so the user's font setting still applies.
body: A preferred value of pure `2.5vw` ignores the user's font size setting at the low end and gives about 9px on a 375px screen. Keep a `rem` part in the middle value and a `rem` minimum.

name: auto-fit card grid
desc: Fits as many cards per row as the container allows and reflows without any media query.
body: `auto-fit` collapses empty tracks, `auto-fill` keeps them. Cards want `auto-fit`. If prices must line up in cards of different heights, make each card `display: flex; flex-direction: column` and give the price `margin-top: auto`.

name: disclosure nav with details
desc: A mobile menu that opens without JavaScript and is keyboard accessible by default.
example:
Menu
  • Rooms
  • Rates

name: scroll offset under a fixed header
desc: Keeps anchor targets visible below a fixed header instead of scrolling them under it.

name: dvh and svh viewport units
desc: Dynamic and small viewport heights, so a full screen panel is not cut off by the mobile browser toolbar.

name: @container
desc: Styles a component by the width of its container, so the same card works in a sidebar and in a wide grid.

name: 375px overflow check
desc: The first rules to add when a phone layout scrolls sideways. Then find the single wide element instead of hiding the overflow.
body: Check at 375px, then at 200 percent zoom, which leaves about 187px of layout width. A page that needs no horizontal scroll at both sizes has no fixed pixel widths left in the hot path.
